body_markdown:
Aston Martin’s DBX SUV has a new derivative that delivers comfort without compromising speed.


The DBX GT has the same powertrain as the[potent S](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/first-drive-2026-aston-martin-dbx-s-adds-aggression-and-loses-weight/) , but is set up to be softer, with a more compliant chassis, less noise, and an even more luxurious cabin.


Starting inside, the seats are redesigned with extra cushioning, including a memory foam layer to shape itself to your posterior. In the back, there are now two individual seats, but still room for a third passenger to perch between them. Quilted panels and deep-pile carpeting add an extra level of luxe. Buyers can choose monotone, duotone, or even tritone upholstery combinations for the semi-aniline leather, while anodized metal controls add some shine.

Noise levels have been cut through additional cabin sealing, refinements to the body structure, and acoustic laminated rear side glass. Apparently, this makes it exactly 13 percent easier to hold a conversation with passengers, take a phone call, or tune into the Bowers & Wilkins audio system.


From the outside, the DBX GT is distinguished by a revised double-vaned grille, a two-piece metal side strake, body-colored aero parts, and new 22-inch forged wheels. The quad exhausts also get a GT-specific polished finish.


Under the hood sits the same 717-hp twin-turbo four-liter V-8 as the DBX S, which the GT matches for straight-line speed, dispatching zero-to-60 mph in 3.1 seconds, and powering on to 193 mph. Stopping power is also from the S, with hefty ceramic discs front and rear. The faster steering rack from the S is installed as well, but when it comes to the suspension tune, the GT goes its own way. The damper settings are revised, and there’s a new damper valve system designed to deliver a more absorbent ride over rough roads. The DBX GT also varies its spring rate depending on which drive mode has been selected.


Further tweaks have been made to the throttle response and the shift feel of the nine-speed wet clutch automatic transmission, dialling back the aggression. The same is true of the exhaust note, which has been tuned in its most mellow setting to eliminate harsh metallic frequencies. Putting the DBX GT in Sport or Sport + modes releases its full voice.


Pricing has yet to be revealed, though deliveries will begin before the end of 2026.
